root_idea.summary: The root expresses bringing something forth into manifestation and scattering or propagating it; a separate lexical branch denotes whiteness or hoariness.
root_idea.development: The bringing-forth branch develops into creating beings and multiplying them, while related Classical Arabic uses preserve sowing, seed, offspring, and scattering. The whiteness branch appears in terms for hoary hair, white salt, and white-marked animals.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied group is an attested Form I Quranic verb and is displayed under the normalized citation form ذَرَأَ.

senses.definition: To create; bring beings or things forth into existence.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic use of bringing created beings into manifestation; context may render it as create or produce.
In the Quranic construction يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ, the multiplication is explained as producing people and cattle in pairs, male and female.
Represented in a reported rare Quranic reading concerning something scattered by the wind; that reading has no supplied QAC word location and is not counted among the six standard QAC occurrences.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sow land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The variant ذَرَا is reported as the more eloquent form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the teeth to fall out of the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The hamzated form is reported alongside forms without hamza and is described by one authority as weak or a mispronunciation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the hair to become white or hoary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The whitening is described especially as beginning in the forepart or upper sides of the head, though the verb is also given more generally for becoming hoary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To anger or provoke someone to anger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV transitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incite, urge, or compel someone to do or undertake something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With بِـ it may mean incite against a person or urge toward an action; with إِلَى it may mean compel someone to have recourse to or do something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make tears flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be a person or a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To frighten someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form IV transitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to cause milk to descend into the udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal form reported as a variant of أَدْرَأَ; the transmitted wording is accompanied by a textual qualification about the direction of the milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In ذَرْءُ النَّارِ, created or destined for the fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantival or passive-participial use of the verbal noun in a fixed expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The offspring of a person, or the number of that person's offspring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions wishing for an increase in someone's progeny.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small amount; somewhat or a little.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a small amount of news, good, or speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something intervening as a separation, barrier, or obstacle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing what stands between two parties or things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whiteness or hoariness, especially in the hair; also whiteness mixed with black.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the beginning or presence of hoary whiteness in the forepart or upper sides of the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely white salt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is derived from ذُرْأَةٌ; a form without hamza is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sown seed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Nominal adjective or participial description of seed that has been sown.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Children or offspring; a collective term that may also be used as a singular.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to the offspring of a man, of men, or of jinn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Progenitors or forebears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Quranic usage in which the term refers to ancestors carried in the laden ark.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred use based on women being the sources of offspring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Creator, used as an epithet of God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial epithet formed from the creating branch of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: White-headed; of certain animals, having a white head or, in another application, ears mottled black and white with the rest of the coat black.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a ram, and in the feminine to a ewe, for whiteness of the head. The mottled-ear sense is applied to a horse or kid, with feminine forms for a female kid or she-goat, and is not applied to sheep-kind.

Frightening is retained as a distinct Form IV meaning.
The dialectal she-camel milk use is retained.
Identifies the infinitive noun and adds no independent lexical branch beyond the verb's creating meaning.

The noun's offspring or offspring-number use is retained.
The amount meaning somewhat or little is retained.
The intervening barrier meaning is retained.
Pointer-only cross-reference.

The adjective for intensely white salt is retained.
The sown-seed noun is retained.
Children or offspring is retained under its own nominal headword.
The progenitor use is retained under the same nominal headword.

The divine Creator epithet is retained.
The animal adjective and its stated application conditions are retained.

cautions: The reported wind-scattering Quranic reading is rare and has no supplied QAC word location; no occurrence location is assigned to it.
Lane reports several variant hamza spellings and evaluates some of them differently; these variants are retained in usage conditions rather than treated as separate Quranic forms.
Lane's Quran quotations for the separate nominal headword ذُرِّيَّةٌ are retained under that headword and are not conflated with the supplied QAC Form I verb.
